locator: §4.1, 'When those words occur in the antecedent of a conditional, or when a person says, ‘I wonder if lying is wrong’ they they are typically not being used to express such disapproval'
interpretation: The datum behind Geach's argument: in the antecedent of a conditional the moral sentence expresses no disapproval; Geach's first premise is one 'one might accept even if one approves of tormenting cats'. The entry says 'typically', so the reading is stated for the one sentence of Geach's example, not for every moral sentence. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
